evidence: AC5: '>= 95% per cell'
a40f ticket operator comment: bedrock sentinel new_ok 11/20, anthropic sentinel 11/20, openai sentinel 19/20 (n=20 per cell)
a40f finding: 'the sentinel directive collapses raw-output layout to 100% prose' — so residual failures are not layout/channel
Plan Approach cites E2 '16/16 compliance across sonnet/haiku on Bedrock' — a different measurement than the a40f 20-per-cell 55%
findings.finding: AC5 predeclares parse success '>= 95% per cell', but the a40f operator-attested run this harness inherits measured parse success under a sentinel directive (which already collapsed layout to 100% prose) at only 11/20 (55%) on anthropic and bedrock, 19/20 (95%) on openai. Since layout was already 100% prose, the residual ~45% failures on anthropic/bedrock are content/validation failures a marker CHANNEL does not address; the plan does not reconcile this with its cited E2 '16/16 compliance' number, so the >=95% threshold may be unachievable or may measure channel-compliance as a proxy for parse-success.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, final [operator-attested] AC line; Approach ('16/16 compliance ... on Bedrock')
scenarios: Operator runs the before/after harness; anthropic and bedrock cells land near their prior ~55% and miss the 95% bar; AC5 cannot be attested and the story stalls despite a correct implementation.
The threshold is quietly reinterpreted as channel-compliance (%prose or %markers-present) rather than parse-success, silently weakening the acceptance bar.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the extraction rule when marker blocks ARE present but the last/all fail parse or validation: whether the parser falls back to the schema-filtered selection pipeline, tries earlier marker blocks, or raises the marker block's validation error (mirroring parse_structured's last-candidate-error behavior), and add a unit pin for it.
evidence: Plan: 'tries marker-delimited blocks FIRST — the LAST marker block wins, validated via validate_to (:177) — and falls back to the selection pipeline for markerless replies'
structured.py:335: 'Candidates passed the screen but none validated — raise the LAST one's error'
ABSENCE: no rule stated for present-but-invalid marker content (fall back to selection? try earlier marker blocks? raise the marker block's validation error?)
findings.finding: The plan specifies marker extraction as 'the LAST marker block wins, validated via validate_to' and that MARKERLESS replies fall through byte-for-byte to the selection pipeline, but is silent on the case where marker(s) ARE present yet the last (or every) marker block fails to parse or fails validation (malformed JSON inside markers, a schema-invalid object, or json-repair-needed content). The existing df3a parse_structured handles the analogous no-valid-candidate case explicitly (raise the last candidate's validation error) and only falls through to tolerant_parse when there are no survivors — the marker path needs an equivalent stated rule.
findings.location: Approach ('the LAST marker block wins, validated via validate_to (:177)'); Scope (structured.py bullet)
scenarios: Model wraps a malformed or schema-invalid object between markers and emits a valid object elsewhere in prose; extraction behavior (marker error vs selection fallback) is undefined, so the implementer picks a policy the pins may not cover.
Marker content needs json-repair (trailing comma): does the marker path invoke tolerant_parse or only plain json.loads, and does failure fall through to the selection pipeline?

findings.suggested_fix: State the marker path as: enumerate marker blocks, validate_to each, select the LAST that validates; if none validate, fall through byte-for-byte to the selection pipeline (mirroring the markerless path) rather than raising.
